setup_notes: Fork main already up to date with upstream. The documented `--stats` flag does not exist on HEAD, so per-stage timings came from the debug build's `run --trace` (summed by /tmp/perfhunt/H1/repro/stages.sh).

hypotheses.title: Every error constructor rebuilds the constant error-detail type map<Cloneable> (twice), defeating subtype memoization in stages 5 and 6
hypotheses.issue: semtypes/error.go:ErrorDetailType returns errorDetailTop(ctx) when the error type is the plain `error` top type, and errorDetailTop ran `NewMappingDefinition().Define(env, nil, CreateCloneable(ctx))` on every call. That built a brand-new mapping definition each time: fresh mapping and cell atoms (about 3 mapping atoms per constructor) and fresh BDD nodes. The atom table is keyed by pointer, so these are never deduplicated. ErrorDetailType runs once per error(...) constructor in stage 5 (type_resolver.go:errorDetailDefaults, from resolveErrorConstructorExpr, which then runs MappingAlternatives on the result) and again in stage 6 (analysis/constructors.go:validateErrorConstructor). Stage 6 then runs AllPossibleMappingFields and per-argument member projections on the result, and finally IsSubtype(providedTy, detailTy). Because detailTy is a new BDD every time, the BDD/subtype memo caches can never be reused across constructors, so each constructor pays for a full mapping subtype check plus the allocations of the rebuild. On the reproducer, validateErrorConstructor was 11% of CPU and 20% of allocated bytes, and errorDetailTop plus errorDetailDefaults were another ~10% of allocations. The type is constant per type Env and should be built once.

reproducer.generator:
import sys
n=int(sys.argv[1])
o=["import ballerina/io;"]
for i in range(n):
    o.append(f"function f{i}(int a) returns error? {{")
    o.append(f"    if a == {i} {{ return error(\"bad{i}\", code = a, reason = \"r\"); }}")
    o.append(f"    if a == {i+1} {{ return error(\"bad{i}b\", code = a); }}")
    o.append(f"    error e = error(\"x\", info = \"y\", n = {i});")
    o.append(f"    return a < 0 ? e : ();")
    o.append("}")
o.append("public function main() { io:println(f0(-1) is error); }")
open(f"errs_{n}.bal","w").write("\n".join(o)+"\n")
reproducer.command: python3 gen_errors.py 5000 > errors_5000.bal; ./bin/benchmark --mode time --runs 10 --warmup 2 --export-summary t.md main <branch> errors_5000.bal (debug build: bal-debug run --trace=t.json errors_5000.bal for per-stage ms)

hypotheses.fix_approach: Add an errorDetail SemType field to semtypes.preallocatedTypeVals, the per-Env struct that already holds the prebuilt json/anydata/cloneable/ordered types. Build it once in newPreallocatedTypeVals as NewMappingDefinition().Define(env, nil, p.cloneable), and make errorDetailTop return it. The value is built during CreateTypeEnv, before the Env is shared, and is read-only afterwards, so no lock is needed (avoid lazy initialization under concurrent stage 5-9 goroutines). Further possible wins not prototyped: have stage 6 reuse stage 5's detail type and defaults, and skip the provided-vs-detail IsSubtype when the detail type is the top map<Cloneable> and each argument was already checked against Cloneable. That second change touches diagnostics, so it needs care to keep messages unchanged.
